title: fix(onboarding): keep shipped .githooks LF for Windows checkouts
body:
## Background

The distributed template ships three POSIX shell files —
`.githooks/_idd-worktree-guard.sh`, `.githooks/pre-commit`, and
`.githooks/pre-push` — to every adopter, in every helper-runtime
profile (they are core entries in `idd-template/ONBOARDING.md`'s
generated file list, not profile-conditional).

This source repository keeps those files LF-only through its own
repository-root `.gitattributes` (`* text=auto eol=lf`). That file is
**not** distributed: it is not in the generated file list, and
`ONBOARDING.md`'s only `.gitattributes` guidance is the
`vendored-node`-only `linguist-vendored` step, which is about language
statistics, not line endings.

The Git for Windows installer's default is
`core.autocrlf=true` ("Checkout Windows-style, commit Unix-style line
endings"). With no adopter-side `.gitattributes` rule, a
native-Windows adopter's working-tree copies of those three files
therefore check out with CRLF.

**Reproduced locally (2026-08-15)** by CRLF-converting the shipped
files and running the hook:

```text
./pre-commit: 6: .: cannot open ./_idd-worktree-guard.sh: No such file
EXIT=2
```

The trailing `\r` becomes part of the sourced path, so
`. "$(dirname "$0")/_idd-worktree-guard.sh"` cannot resolve. The hook
does not silently do nothing — it exits non-zero, so **every commit and
push in a repository with `core.hooksPath` wired is hard-blocked** with
an error message that names a file that visibly exists.

Two aggravating details, both verified against current `main`:

- `idd-doctor` reports the guard as **wired** in that broken state.
  `hookWiresWorktreeGuard` in `src/scripts/idd-doctor.mts` matches
  `/^[ \t]*(?:\.|source)[ \t]+[^\n]*_idd-worktree-guard\.sh/m`, which
  still matches a CRLF line because the `\r` sits after the match. So
  the one diagnostic an adopter would run reports green while git
  cannot execute the hook at all.
- The guard is otherwise CRLF-aware for *input* it reads
  (`tr -d ' \t\r\n'` when parsing `.github/idd/config.json`) but not
  for its own file bytes.

A `*.sh` rule alone is insufficient: `pre-commit` and `pre-push` are
extensionless, so they need an explicit path rule.

No existing issue covers this. Related but distinct: #1951 / PR #1969
covered hook-manager coexistence (`core.hooksPath` being reset by
Husky), a different failure mode with a different fix.

## Proposed change

1. Add a line-ending step to `idd-template/ONBOARDING.md`'s
   worktree-guard activation section instructing the adopter to add an
   explicit LF rule covering all three shipped hook files (for example
   a `.githooks/* text eol=lf` entry) to their own `.gitattributes`
   before or while enabling `core.hooksPath`, with a one-line note that
   Git for Windows' default `core.autocrlf=true` otherwise hard-blocks
   every commit.
2. Extend `idd-doctor`'s worktree-guard wiring check so a hook file
   whose bytes contain `\r\n` is reported as a distinct, actionable
   not-wired/broken state rather than passing `hookWiresWorktreeGuard`.
   Keep the message specific enough to name the line-ending cause and
   the `.gitattributes` remedy.

Both halves belong together: (1) prevents the state, (2) stops the
diagnostic from certifying it as healthy when it already exists.

## Acceptance criteria

- `idd-template/ONBOARDING.md`'s worktree-guard section documents an
  explicit LF `.gitattributes` rule covering all three shipped
  `.githooks/` files, names the extensionless-filename reason a `*.sh`
  rule is insufficient, and names Git for Windows' default
  `core.autocrlf=true` as the trigger.
- `idd-doctor` reports a CRLF-containing `.githooks/pre-commit`,
  `.githooks/pre-push`, or `_idd-worktree-guard.sh` as not correctly
  wired, with a message naming line endings as the cause. Verified by a
  test in `tests/` that feeds CRLF hook content through the wiring
  check and asserts the non-wired verdict, alongside an unchanged LF
  case.
- The LF case's existing verdict and message are byte-identical to
  today's — this adds a failing state, it does not change any passing
  one.
- `node scripts/sync-docs.mjs --apply` produces no diff beyond the
  intended edit, and `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` passes.
- `pnpm run lint:minimum` and `pnpm run test` pass.

## Candidate files

- `idd-template/ONBOARDING.md`
- `src/scripts/idd-doctor.mts` (and its generated
  `scripts/idd-doctor.mjs`)
- a test file under `tests/`

## Out of scope

- Shipping a `.gitattributes` file into adopter repositories. An
  adopter's `.gitattributes` is theirs to own; overwriting or creating
  one during import is a separate decision.
- Any change to the guard's own logic, branch matching, or opt-in gate.
- The guard's process-fork count on Windows (tracked separately).
